gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Woodgod arrives with a vintage, commanding swagger. Noto Sans PhagsPa follows in a contemporary, approachable voice, its curves open enough to see through, so the heading gets its drama while the text stays easygoing.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-phoenici: Vintage muscle, loudly stated. Woodgod stands up top with tall lowercase nearly matching its capitals, while Noto Sans Phoenician sits below it as a modern plain sans, its s curves opening wide at both ends.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-runic: Woodgod's wide channel into every bowl is what you notice first. Noto Sans Runic backs it with a big x-height and curves that never close up, so a modest heading size lets the text carry its share.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-saurasht: Noto Sans Saurashtra is a clean sans whose capitals barely rise above their neighbors. And Woodgod above it is the loud one, vintage and commanding, so the text can stay quietly connected and open to the outside.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Commanding, in a vintage way. Woodgod does the shouting with its tall lowercase nearly touching the capitals, while Noto Sans Sunuwar, a plain sans, does the explaining with curves that leave daylight.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri reads clean and businesslike. Woodgod brings a vintage, commanding weight above it, and the sans-serif text with its tall x-height and short ascenders keeps the page moving beneath.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac has bowls like blown glass bulbs. Woodgod is best at commanding attention with a wide channel into every bowl, while the plain sans is best at easy, modern turns in its s shapes.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Vintage and loud, a proper show-off. Woodgod takes the heading with its commanding tall lowercase, and Noto Sans Syriac Western follows as a clean sans-serif whose terminals sit well away from the stroke body.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa reads clean and modern, its lowercase filling most of the height. Woodgod is best at vintage command, and the plain sans is best at open curves with clear gaps.
